recipes.name: Best Breakfast Pizza
ingredients_raw: 1 cup frozen hash brown potatoes, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Meanwhile, cook sausage in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until evenly browned. Drain, crumble, and set aside.

Separate crescent roll dough into 8 triangles. Place on an ungreased 12-inch pizza pan with points toward the center; press dough together to form a crust. Bottom crust should be sealed and outside edge should be slightly raised.
Spoon sausage over crust; sprinkle with hash browns and top with Cheddar cheese.
Beat eggs, milk, salt, and black pepper together in a bowl; pour over crust. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until eggs are set, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Breakfast Pizza
raw_recipe.description: This breakfast pizza recipe uses refrigerated crescent roll dough, sausage, hash browns, and cheese to make a different kind of breakfast. It is the best.

review.reviewBody:
This ended up being a fantastic recipe - once I gave up on the idea of trying to make it on a pizza pan! I laid out the crescent roll pieces on a pizza pan and could tell pretty quickly it wasn't going to be easy to make a circle that covered the pan. So I took the suggestion of using a 9x13 and coaxed the pieces into fitting with a little help from my rolling pin. I also took the suggestion of baking the crescent roll crust for a few minutes (6min?) before adding the toppings - VERY helpful!

Other changes I made included using Morningstar Griller crumbles instead of sausage to make it vegetarian and using a Mexican 3 cheese blend to add a little kick. I didn't brown the crumbles because they seem to cook just fine even when added frozen, but I did the brown the hash browns, just for good measure.

I still baked it for 25 min even though I had pre-baked the crust a little, and let it sit for a few minutes before serving. It was EXCELLENT!!

I didn't actually plan to make this recipe, so I didn't shop for it. I used this recipe as a guide to make a breakfast casserole in a 9" pie dish this morning (I didn't have a pizza pan the right size). I only had hash brown patties on hand, so I precooked those and chopped them up. They stuck up from the eggs and were nice and crispy. Again, I didn't have parmesan, so I used a mix of mozzarella and sharp cheddar. I also added onions to the sausage when I cooked it. Due to other reviews that also made changes, I did bake the crust 6-7 minutes before I topped it and was glad I did. Family loved it. Good topped with gravy!

Great recipe. I do in a sm. rectangle pan, 9 x 13. Lay crescent dough in greased pan like a sheet (they do make dough sheets too if u can find them). It says thawed hash browns. I fry about 2 cups briefly before adding. No mushiness. Also add green pepper, crumbled bacon, lots of pepper, and more cheese. Easy cut squares. A go to recipe around here.

First time I made it before it was done I said “never again!” Then I tasted it...AMAZING! This recipe can be quite messy especially inside your oven. Recommend that what whatever you cook it on has sides to contain leakage. I also used about a pack and a half of crescent rolls the first time (round) and then 2 the next time in a rectangle. I didn’t even separate dough just pushed all perforations together. 
Lastly, even the first time I made it I was wary of putting raw potatoes into the the mixture and only cooking a short time so I threw them in a pan for 5 min and cooked them slightly letting them finish in the oven. This way you can control the desired crispyness of them. This is a delicious and simple recipe. Enjoy

I made this for a get together with some friends. Everyone thought it was fantastic! I made a few modifications. I used 2 cans of crescent rolls to cover a 15 inch pizza pan using the same method of separating the triangles. I did overlap the points in the center, 1/2 inch approximate. I placed a piece of parchment paper to make the pizza slide right off the pan. I had enough dough to roll the edges slightly to make a pretty crust.

I also microwaved a 3 medium potatoes till tender and ran them under cold water just to cool them. I peeled and roughly chopped them placed them

I braught down servings to 7, followed the recipe to the letter BUT I added 5 eggs total mixed with 5tbsp milk , salt and pepper. I put into a 9" pie crust and the result was great and very easy to make.

I have made this recipe for YEARS as our Christmas morning breakfast. (It's been a tradition longer than that in my husband's family.) For those having issues with the eggs "offloading," you can use one less egg and it still turns out wonderfully. Also, I have learned that pouring the eggs in before putting the cheese on top makes a big difference. The best pan I've made this in is a tart pan with a removable bottom--it makes it easier to cut when serving.

This turned out really well! I used a glass pie baking dish instead of a pizza tray, because I read that some other reviewers had trouble keeping the eggs from running over. About 5-10 minutes from it being finished in the oven, I brushed the outer crust with maple syrup. It was a good move....so yummy.

I was looking for a recipe to use with my new Pampered Chef stone and decided to try this one! Turned out great! I had to use one and a half crescent roll packages and 9 eggs, with a little more milk. It was a hit with the whole family! And it isn’t easy making five kids happy at the same time, lol! Today we are adding diced ham with the sausage!

I made this in a pie pan, so I actually made about half. Still used 5 eggs should have used 4. I used half a roll of sausage. Some bacon bits, green onion, and bell pepper. I used shredded potatoes for my hash browns. Added shredded cheese, then the egg -milk mix. Cooked @375 degrees for 30 min. Perfect.

Great dish, my husband and children really enjoyed it. I added sage to the sausage. Removed sausage from skillet and cooked the hash browns with some dried onion flakes in the same pan just until they started to brown. Used grated cheddar and Mozzarella cheese. Added Italian seasoning, salt and pepper to 7 eggs. baked the dough for 6 min. before adding toppings, next time I will only go about 4 min. Will absolutely make again.
Awesome ❣️ I used a deep dish pan worked well and so yummy and EASY 🧑‍🍳
I think maybe I didn’t have enough sausage. It was very bland.

It was good but it needed a little more. I baked it following recipe. Instead of a pizza pan I used a 13x9 pan. It definitely needed a little more seasoning next time I would add bell pepper and onion. Other than that it was good.
I made in a rectangular dish instead of a pizza pan. There was a lot of liquid in the bottom which was a real disappointment but it still tasted awesome. Likely from the cheese oil...

I substituted Italian ground sausage for added flavor. One-half cup each of sautéed onions and red peppers were added also. The breakfast pizza was for a breakfast baby shower - everyone loved it and several asked for the recipe. Next time I'll use turkey sausage, low fat cheese, and try a whole wheat dough to make the dish a little more healthy and reduce the fat.

I followed the directions exactly with the correct measurements and it was awful. The egg oozed out EVERYWHERE because there was just too much. The hashbrowns never browned and my crust burned because I was waiting for them to brown. Definitely won’t be making this again.
I added diced brown sugar ham, used maple sausage, and topped with bacon crumbles. It's my all time favorite breakfast!
I’ve made this for probably the last 30 years on Christmas morning and still making it and love it. Can make night before except for the egg and milk mixture.

My kids and I made this but at the last minute so we put time potatoes instead of sausage and in a big dish, since we do not have a pizza pan and we used biscuits instead of croissants (sorry we had to improvise with what we had) and we sprinkled bacon on top and it was FANTASTIC!!!
